primary_diagnosis: Diabetic nephropathy (type 2 diabetes mellitus related chronic kidney disease)
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient presents with insulin‑treated type 2 diabetes, microalbuminuria, and a markedly reduced eGFR, establishing diabetic nephropathy as the most probable cause of his CKD. Long‑standing, poorly controlled hypertension with target‑organ damage (CKD stage 3b) constitutes a second major contributor. His refractory blood pressure, young age, and lack of ACE‑I/ARB therapy raise concern for secondary hypertension, which warrants dedicated evaluation. An isolated creatinine of 7.6 mg/dL suggests a possible superimposed AKI, while chronic anemia aligns with CKD‑related erythropoietin deficiency. Lesser‑probability considerations include primary glomerulonephritis and NAFLD, supported only by proteinuria and metabolic risk factors, respectively. Unresolved findings (outlier creatinine, urine bilirubin, implausible HbA1c, missing BMI/lipids) highlight data gaps that must be addressed to refine probabilities.
unresolved_findings: Serum creatinine 7.6 mg/dL (single outlier, possible lab error)
Positive urine bilirubin without accompanying liver function tests
Absence of BMI, lipid panel, and recent fasting glucose/HbA1c values
recommended_workup: Repeat serum creatinine and calculate eGFR (preferably using CKD‑EPI) to confirm renal function
Quantitative urine albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio (UACR) to assess proteinuria severity
Comprehensive metabolic panel including liver enzymes (AST, ALT, ALP, GGT, bilirubin) to evaluate urine bilirubin finding
Repeat HbA1c or obtain fasting plasma glucose to verify diabetic control
Lipid profile (total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides) for cardiovascular risk stratification
BMI measurement and waist circumference to assess obesity/metabolic syndrome
Complete blood count with iron studies, reticulocyte count, and erythropoietin level to characterize anemia
Renal ultrasound to evaluate structural kidney disease
Screen for secondary causes of hypertension (aldosterone‑renin ratio, renal‑artery imaging, sleep study for OSA)
Medication reconciliation focusing on NSAIDs, herbal supplements, and recent contrast exposure
Urine microscopy (RBC casts, dysmorphic RBCs, WBCs) to rule in/out glomerulonephritis
Echocardiogram to assess for cardiorenal syndrome
